note_body: Jesus asks how David's son can be David's Lord, and from the throne He finally answers it Himself — I am the root and the offspring of David. Before David and from David, both at once.
lens_gloss: son, offspring and heir — the riddle stands until you meet the Son who is also David's Lord.

note_body: Isaiah watched a Servant whose soul was made an offering for sin; Jesus steps into that prophecy by name — the Son of Man serving, and paying, until many go free.
lens_gloss: ransom — the price paid to set a captive free; one life laid down so that many go out liberated.

note_body: Jesus pays a tax He does not owe rather than trip up watching hearts, and Paul carries the same care — giving no offence in any thing. Real freedom bends low so the ministry is not blamed.
lens_gloss: to set a stumbling stone, to trip someone up — the harm Jesus takes practical, humble care to avoid.

note_body: After a day of being tested, Jesus becomes the asker, and Mark sets the same question in the temple courts. His questions are not traps but doorways, walking hearers toward who the Christ really is.
lens_gloss: to question with purpose — the Teacher's asking that opens a heart rather than springing a trap.

note_body: Daniel saw one like the Son of Man riding the clouds to the Ancient of Days; Jesus claims that night vision as His own return. The hope has a name and a face.
lens_gloss: glory — weight and radiance made visible; the splendor belonging to God, seen at last upon the returning Son.

note_body: Isaiah pleads, why spend for what never satisfies — come, eat what is good; the king in Jesus' parable sends the same word with the feast steaming. All things are ready, and the invitation is love.
lens_gloss: wedding feast — the kingdom pictured not as a courtroom summons but a marriage table, spread and steaming.

note_body: Paul sees differing ministries all answering to the same Lord; Jesus guards the truth underneath — titles may vary, but only Christ is the Guide who forms the soul.
lens_gloss: guide, way-leading teacher — a title used only here in the New Testament, and reserved by Jesus for Christ alone.

note_body: Job saw it long ago: God disappoints the devices of the crafty so their hands cannot finish the scheme. In the temple court, one coin and one sentence from Jesus do exactly that — and the trappers leave marveling.
lens_gloss: to give back what is owed — the coin bears Caesar's image, but the soul bears God's.

note_body: When Jehu was anointed, every man snatched off his garment and laid it under him, because that is what you do when a king is announced. Jerusalem's coats and branches say the same thing — and this King is worth everything we lay down.
lens_gloss: to spread out beneath — what you own, laid down under the feet of the King you crown.

note_title: The waiting ones get their day.
note_body: Isaiah hears a future people say, "Lo, this is our God; we have waited for him, and he will save us." "Even so, come, Lord Jesus" is that same waiting, leaning forward on a promise He signed Himself.
lens_gloss: I am coming — His present-tense promise; the church takes the very same word and turns it into a prayer: Come.

note_body: Joseph made himself strange and spoke roughly while his heart was breaking with love for his brothers. Jesus' silence toward the crying mother is that same kind of strange — a delay with mercy already moving behind it.
lens_gloss: to cry out, raw and loud — the unpolished plea that His silence tests but never despises.

note_title: He says the word Himself: compassion.
note_body: Matthew lets us hear what Mark's scene holds: "I have compassion on the multitude... I will not send them away fasting." The Lord who counts your three days of staying near also counts the miles home — He will not let you faint on the way.
lens_gloss: to call close to oneself — before the miracle, Jesus draws His helpers near to share His compassion.

note_title: The city asks; the prophet answers.
note_body: Jerusalem's question, "Who is this?" was answered before it was asked — Isaiah saw One coming in glorious apparel, "mighty to save." Familiarity asks a shallow question; prophecy hands back the deep answer.
lens_gloss: to shake as an earthquake shakes — His arrival rattles a whole city into asking who He really is.

note_body: Took, blessed, broke, gave — the motions over five loaves are the motions over the bread of remembrance. The hands that would not despise a small lunch would not withhold His own body; nothing offered to those hands stays small.
lens_gloss: to speak a good word over — He blesses the small offering before His hands make it enough.

note_body: In their tents Israel murmured, "Because the LORD hated us, he brought us out of Egypt" — fear can retell even redemption as cruelty. The one-talent servant does the same, and both stories warn us that distance lets fear paint a false Master.
lens_gloss: hard, dried stiff — the rigid picture fear paints of a Master who was never harsh.

note_title: An old idol, borrowed for slander.
note_body: Beelzebub was Ekron's idol, the god sick King Ahaziah sought instead of the LORD. The scribes reach back for that same borrowed name to explain the Son of God — a threatened heart would rather credit Ekron than bend the knee.
lens_gloss: to drive out, expel — the liberating power at work is the very thing the scribes renamed darkness.

note_body: The verse Matthew reaches for is Isaiah's Servant song: "Behold my servant, whom I uphold... he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles." The quiet, understated work of Jesus is not random; it is a seven-century-old promise keeping its appointment.
lens_gloss: to fill full — in Jesus, prophecy is not merely matched; it is filled to the brim with its meaning.

note_title: A Master in heaven, just and equal.
note_body: Paul tells earthly masters to give "that which is just and equal," because they answer to a Master in heaven. The vineyard owner's "whatsoever is right I will give you" is that heavenly Master's own character — you can enter the field before every detail is measured.
lens_gloss: just, right — the wage rests on the Master's righteous character, not on the worker's bargaining.

note_body: King Jeroboam's stiffened hand needed a prophet to entreat the LORD before it was "restored him again." In the synagogue Jesus does not intercede — He commands, and the hand is whole; the Restorer Himself has stepped into the room.
lens_gloss: to restore to its first condition — His command gives back what withering took, whole as the other.

note_body: Jesus tells His host to invite "the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind" — guests who cannot repay. The wedding hall of the parable fills the same way, and so does the kingdom: by servants who carry the King's welcome past the expected list.
lens_gloss: to gather into one — the root of 'synagogue'; His servants make a congregation out of the highways.

note_title: Not our righteousness, but Your mercies.
note_body: Daniel prays, "we do not present our supplications before thee for our righteousnesses, but for thy great mercies" — and the Canaanite mother stands in exactly that posture. Humble persistence never argues its worthiness; it banks everything on how merciful He is.
lens_gloss: a little crumb — the diminutive of small; she trusts that even the least of His mercy is enough.

note_title: God's law made room for hunger.
note_body: Long before the Pharisees kept watch, God wrote provision into His own law: a hungry traveler could eat grapes to the full in a neighbor's vineyard. The disciples were inside God's mercy the whole time — the scrutiny came from men, never from Him.
lens_gloss: to pluck, pull off — an ordinary hungry gesture that men judged and the Lord of the Sabbath defended.

note_body: Nebuchadnezzar's dream-tree sheltered beasts and birds and fed all flesh — and pride brought it down. The mustard seed grows slower and smaller-looking, but the shelter mercy builds is the one that lasts.
lens_gloss: to pitch a tent, to nest — the small seed grows into a place where weary wings can settle and stay.

note_body: Paul names what he was — "a blasphemer, and a persecutor" — and then testifies, "I obtained mercy, because I did it ignorantly in unbelief." The warning is for hearts hardened against the Spirit's witness; Paul is living proof that a reachable heart is never past mercy.
lens_gloss: to slander, speak against — not a tender heart's stumble but a settled speaking-against the Spirit's witness.

note_body: The words Matthew quotes from Isaiah — beloved, well pleased — Peter heard spoken audibly from heaven on the holy mount. Before the Servant proved anything, the Father was already delighted; beloved identity is where the serving starts.
lens_gloss: beloved — the Father's name for the Servant before any work is weighed; service flows out of being loved.

note_body: The apostle who heard Jesus name how Gentile rulers "exercise lordship" hands the correction to every elder: "neither as being lords over God's heritage, but being ensamples to the flock." Kingdom influence protects and models; it never presses down.
lens_gloss: to lord it down upon — power pressed from above; the same word Peter later forbids among Christ's shepherds.

note_title: Rivers of tears over unkept mercy.
note_body: The psalmist's eyes run like rivers "because they keep not thy law" — grief over another's hardness, carried straight to God. The fellowservants do the same with the unmerciful servant: a sorrow that refuses to gossip and goes to the lord instead.
lens_gloss: to be grieved, pained — mercy refused wounds the whole household, and holy grief carries it to the lord.

note_title: The Servant's manner, every servant's rule.
note_body: Isaiah's Servant "shall not strive, nor cry," and Paul turns it into a standing order: "the servant of the Lord must not strive; but be gentle unto all men." Quiet strength is not a personality type — it is the family resemblance.
lens_gloss: to quarrel, to wrangle — the Servant's strength never needs a shouting match to prove itself.

note_title: He was always in the water.
note_body: "When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee" — Israel carried that promise for centuries. On Galilee it stops being a figure of speech: the Lord of the promise is bodily in the storm, saying, "It is I; be not afraid."
lens_gloss: take heart, have courage — not courage self-mustered, but courage handed to the fearful by the One who speaks it.

note_body: David marvels that God crowned frail humanity "with glory and honour," a little lower than the angels. Jesus does the arithmetic of that crown: if not one cheap sparrow falls unnoticed, the child God crowned need not decide anything out of fear.
lens_gloss: to outweigh, surpass — in the Father's scales you outweigh whole flocks; fear loses its arithmetic.

note_body: The psalm says God gives food "to the young ravens which cry" — the least glamorous mouths in creation, fed on schedule. Jesus takes it further: five sparrows sell for two farthings, yet not one of them is forgotten before God — and neither is the concern you keep calling too small.
lens_gloss: to forget — even the fifth sparrow the market throws in free, heaven's memory never lets slip.

note_title: The Psalm names who stills seas.
note_body: "Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them" — the psalmist is describing the LORD alone. When the wind quits the moment Jesus enters the boat, the boat is holding the One the Psalm was about.
lens_gloss: to grow weary, die down — the storm itself tires out and quits the moment He steps into the boat.

note_body: Paul dares to say it is "given" to believers — granted as a grace — not only to believe on Christ but also to suffer for His sake. The councils and courtrooms Jesus foretold are not the end of the witness; they are where the witness happens.
lens_gloss: to hand over — the Gospels' own word for Jesus' betrayal; His witnesses walk a road their Master walked first.

note_body: God told Israel through Isaiah, "Ye are my witnesses... my servant whom I have chosen." On Patmos, John is that word come true — a life bearing record of what it has seen of Jesus, which is what every following life quietly does.
lens_gloss: witness, testimony — the root of 'martyr'; what John saw became something his whole life carried.

note_body: Jesus said the gospel "shall be preached in all the world for a witness"; in Acts He tells us how — "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you." The worldwide witness is Spirit-carried, and it starts as near as your own Jerusalem.
lens_gloss: to herald, cry out publicly — kingdom news is carried like a town crier's announcement until every nation hears.

note_body: When Israel pushed Samuel away, God told him the rejection had landed on heaven itself; Jesus turns that same truth toward the door of welcome — receive the one He sends, and you have received the Lord who sent him.
lens_gloss: to receive, to welcome as a guest — hospitality that takes a person in as one's own, and finds Christ in the doorway.

note_title: The bush still speaks present tense.
note_body: At the bush that burned and was not consumed, God spoke His name in the present tense — I am, not I was — the God of Abraham. Jesus takes the Sadducees back to that fire and shows resurrection standing in the grammar.
lens_gloss: to waken, to raise up — the Gospels' resurrection word; the dead rise as sleepers roused by a living voice.

note_body: Jeremiah watched people stand at the crossroads, see the good way, and answer, 'We will not walk therein.' Jesus grieves the same refusal in leaders who watched publicans and harlots run past them into righteousness and still would not move.
lens_gloss: to change one's mind with regret afterward — the turning the leaders withheld even after watching grace transform sinners.

note_body: Jesus lets the accusers' own sons stand as their judges, and Paul says God's law finishes the work — it speaks until every defending mouth is stopped and the heart admits its scales were never even.
lens_gloss: a judge, one who weighs a matter and renders verdict — here the accusers' own sons hold the scales against them.

note_title: A king who felt like a child.
note_body: Solomon wore a crown and still told God, 'I am but a little child; I know not how to go out or come in.' Jesus sets a real child among His disciples to teach the posture that ambition had crowded out.
lens_gloss: a little child — small, unranked, openly dependent; the living picture Jesus places at the center of ambitious men.

note_body: The words spoken over Isaac — thy son, thine only son, whom thou lovest — walk up the hill again in this parable. Only this time the Father does not stay the hand; the wellbeloved Son is truly given.
lens_gloss: beloved, dearly loved — the Father's own baptismal word over Jesus, given here to the son sent last.

note_title: One house before the whole world.
note_body: Ezekiel was not handed the nations; he was told to go to one house and speak the words given him. Jesus shows the Twelve the same mercy — a focused path for today, not the whole world in one breath.
lens_gloss: to send out with commission and authority — the root of 'apostle'; a defined errand, not a vague burden.

note_title: Darkness is only a sitting place.
note_body: Micah answers his enemy from the ground: when I sit in darkness, the LORD shall be a light unto me. Revelation finishes his sentence — a city with no night at all, where God Himself is the lamp forever.
lens_gloss: to give light, to illumine — God Himself replacing sun and lamp, shining directly upon His servants forever.

note_title: Rise; He is calling for thee.
note_body: The same message finds a blind beggar by the Jericho road and a grieving sister in Bethany: the Master is calling for thee. Both rise, because a need brought honestly to Jesus is never an interruption.
lens_gloss: take heart, be of good courage — the word carried from Jesus to a man about to be truly seen.

note_body: Urijah preached the word and a king cut him down, casting his body among the common graves; John's head is taken in a prison. Scripture refuses to look away from either, and neither sorrow falls outside God's remembering.
lens_gloss: a prison, a guarded place — John ends his faithful course unseen by crowds, yet never unseen by God.

note_body: Moses heard it first — 'Who made thee a prince and a judge over us?' — and Jesus hears its echo in the temple courts. In both cases the answer was never a committee's approval, but the God who sent them.
lens_gloss: authority, rightful power — not seized or borrowed but given; the leaders demand its source while standing before it.

note_body: Paul hands the Roman church the same two-sided coin Jesus gave the Twelve: wise unto that which is good, simple concerning evil. Wisdom reads the wolves clearly; innocence refuses to learn their ways.
lens_gloss: unmixed, unalloyed — dove-pure; innocence that keeps no trace of the wolf's cunning blended in.

note_body: Peter's one-sentence memory of the whole story — He went about doing good and healing, for God was with Him — is already visible by that sea, where Jesus steps back from danger without stepping back from compassion.
lens_gloss: to withdraw, to make room — a deliberate stepping aside that protects the mission without abandoning the people.

note_body: God shows Isaiah hidden things and then presses him: 'Will not ye declare it?' Jesus builds the same movement into His disciples — what is whispered in the dark place is being prepared for daylight, not for storage.
lens_gloss: to herald, to proclaim aloud like a town crier — private hearing turned into public announcement from the rooftops.

note_body: Mark tells us Jesus spoke in parables 'as they were able to hear it' — mercy in the very method. The story slips past our raised defenses and turns on the light only as fast as the heart can bear it.
lens_gloss: a placing alongside — a story laid next to life so the heart can see itself before it raises a shield.

note_title: A small errand, a prophetic hill.
note_body: Zechariah saw the mount of Olives split under the feet of the coming King; Mark shows two disciples sent from that same hill to fetch a colt. The ordinary errand and the everlasting purpose stand on the same ground.
lens_gloss: to draw near, approach — Jerusalem and the cross are close now, yet the next step is a simple errand.

note_title: Jeremiah's lost sheep get a Seeker.
note_body: Jeremiah grieved that God's people had become lost sheep, scattered by shepherds who forgot them. Jesus takes up the very phrase and sends the Twelve as the search party mercy had always intended.
lens_gloss: to be lost, perishing — strayed past all self-rescue; the word explains why someone had to be sent.

note_title: Grace at both ends of the story.
note_body: Paul says grace found us dead and quickened us together with Christ; John closes the whole Bible with the same word. What quickened you at the beginning is the blessing that walks you home.
lens_gloss: grace — favor freely given, never earned wages; the Bible's chosen final word to its readers.

note_body: Paul and Barnabas obey this instruction to the letter — they shake the dust of a refusing city from their feet and walk straight on to Iconium. Rejection stays at the gate; the calling travels on.
lens_gloss: road-dust kicked up by travel — the only thing a rejecting city leaves on a disciple, and even that is shaken off.

note_body: A nobleman in Cana and a kneeling father at the mountain's foot come the same way — parents who stop managing appearances and carry a suffering child straight to Jesus. Plain need is a doorway He honors.
lens_gloss: to fall on one's knees — the body's honest prayer; pretense cannot survive that posture.

note_body: The scribes' teaching rests on Malachi's promise that Elijah would come before the great day of the LORD. The disciples carry that very text up to Jesus, and He opens the prophecy instead of shaming the question.
lens_gloss: it is necessary, it must be — Scripture's word for God's appointed order, which Jesus confirms and Himself fulfills.

note_body: Years later Jesus audits these very orders: 'When I sent you without purse... lacked ye any thing?' Their answer — 'Nothing' — is the testimony that obedience never had to wait on a full wallet.
lens_gloss: to acquire, to procure for oneself — the gathering Jesus halts; His mission runs on His supply, not stockpiles.

note_title: He ate, rose, and walked away.
note_body: Esau despised his birthright without a speech — he ate, drank, rose up, and went his way. The invited guests do the same, letting a farm and a ledger outweigh the feast of a King.
lens_gloss: to neglect, to shrug without caring — refusal that needs no hostility; the quiet no that still declines a King.

note_body: Isaiah dared to ask whether prey can be taken from the mighty, and God promised even the captives of the terrible shall be delivered. In Mark, the Stronger One walks in, binds the strong man, and carries the captives home.
lens_gloss: strong, mighty — the tyrant's proud title, held only until the Stronger One steps through his door.

note_body: The collectors are asking after Moses' old half-shekel for the sanctuary — an obligation as ordinary as a yearly bill. Jesus meets it with unhurried peace, and the true Temple pays the temple's tax.
lens_gloss: the double-drachma temple tax — an ordinary yearly bill that becomes a doorway into Jesus' unhurried provision.

note_body: Decades after this parable, Jesus sends the same image to a drowsy church in Sardis: watch, remember, hold fast. The thief-in-the-night warning was never meant to frighten His people — only to keep their lamps tended.
lens_gloss: master of the house — the one answerable under his own roof; watchfulness is an owner taking his charge seriously.

note_body: Jesus said a servant is left in the dark but friends are told what the Master is doing. So when Revelation is given 'to shew unto his servants' what must come, the label says servant — and the treatment says friend.
lens_gloss: an unveiling, a drawing back of the curtain — Jesus lifting the veil so His own need not guess in the dark.

note_body: The Sadducees try to fold resurrection into this world's arithmetic, and Isaiah already knew why the frame would fail: His thoughts are not our thoughts. Peace begins where our categories end and His larger mind is trusted.
lens_gloss: a standing up again — resurrection; a life too large for this age's categories, and no less certain for it.

note_body: In the temple court Jesus reads the trap behind the flattery, and Hebrews says plainly why — all things are naked and opened before His eyes. His peace does not come from not seeing; it comes from seeing everything and standing steady anyway.
lens_gloss: stage-acting, wearing a mask; Jesus reads the performance behind the flattering question and stays unshaken.

note_title: Peter counts; Christ becomes the measure.
note_body: Peter wants a number he can keep, and Colossians quietly takes the arithmetic away — "even as Christ forgave you, so also do ye." The measure of mercy is not a count but a Person.
lens_gloss: to release, send away, let go — forgiveness as loosening your grip on a debt someone owes you.

note_body: What Jesus asks the rich young ruler in love, He asks every follower on the road — deny yourself, take up the cross, come. Release is not a special assignment for the wealthy; it is the shape of following.
lens_gloss: to love with willed, self-giving devotion; the call to release flows from a love that first beheld him.

note_body: Jesus is not inventing this sorrow — He is quoting Micah, who watched households turn on each other centuries before. The prophet named the wound; the Son walks into it with us, refusing any peace built on pretending.
lens_gloss: to cleave in two — His truth divides what false peace had merely glued together.

note_title: An upper room in every greeting.
note_body: The peace Peter breathes over the churches is the very peace Jesus willed to His own the night before the cross — "my peace I give unto you." Every holy greeting since has been passing that inheritance from hand to hand.
lens_gloss: wholeness and well-being, shalom in Greek dress, spoken over the whole family that is in Christ.

note_title: Old hands, young heads, one blessing.
note_body: Jacob crossed his hands over his grandsons' heads to bless them, and centuries later parents are still bringing children for holy hands. The disciples saw an interruption; heaven saw the oldest tradition in the family.
lens_gloss: a little child, small and dependent — precisely the ones the Kingdom refuses to call an interruption.

note_title: The prophets' road, the Son's road.
note_body: Stephen asks a question with only one answer — which of the prophets was not persecuted? — and Jesus told His disciples the same coming down the mountain. Being misunderstood does not mean being off the path; it may mean you are on the well-worn one.
lens_gloss: "it stands written" — even the mistreatment of God's messengers never fell outside God's script.

note_body: The Jesus who slipped away by ship after hard news is the same one who tells His weary friends, "Come ye yourselves apart... and rest a while." He does not only permit the pause — He prescribes it.
lens_gloss: a lonely, uncrowded place — room enough for grief to breathe before the crowds find you again.

note_body: When Moses gathered Israel to hear the law, the little ones were named on the guest list — men, women, children, and the stranger. Jesus is not starting something new at the roadside; He is restoring a welcome written in from the beginning.
lens_gloss: to hinder or block the way; Jesus commands the hurried to stop standing between children and Himself.

note_body: God warned Jeremiah that even his own brothers would speak fair words and deal treacherously — and Jesus tells His disciples the same hard truth without flinching. Faithfulness sometimes costs the approval of the people closest to us, and the Lord says so in advance so it will not break us.
lens_gloss: a member of one's own household — the ache of division wearing the most familiar face.

note_body: At Mamre the LORD asked, "Is any thing too hard for the LORD?" — and the question hung open over the generations like a door. Looking straight at His stunned disciples, Jesus walks through it: with God all things are possible.
lens_gloss: possible, within power; what ends human calculation still sits easily inside the strength of God.

note_title: The bush still burns in Patmos.
note_body: The Name given to Moses — I AM THAT I AM — comes to the seven churches as "him which is, and which was, and which is to come." Grace and peace stand on the God who was never becoming and will never stop being.
lens_gloss: "the One who is" — John bends Greek grammar to echo the burning bush's Name, I AM.

note_body: The man face-down in the dirt of Matthew 17 is the elder writing decades later, "we were with him in the holy mount." What frightened Peter that day became the memory that steadied him for life — holy fear, kept long enough, turns into testimony.
lens_gloss: to fear, to be gripped by awe — the trembling holy nearness wakes before mercy's touch lifts it.

note_title: A weaned child, a quieted soul.
note_body: David describes the very posture Jesus requires — a soul that has stopped striving and leans, satisfied, like a weaned child against its mother. Receiving the kingdom is not a performance; it is that leaning.
lens_gloss: to receive, to welcome as a gift — the kingdom cannot be earned or seized, only accepted.

note_body: Seven hundred years before, Isaiah watched for the Servant who would not break what was bruised or quench what barely smoked. Matthew looks at Jesus and says plainly: this is Him — the gentleness was promised by name.
lens_gloss: to crush or bruise; cracked but not severed — the Servant's hands are safe for what is nearly broken.

note_title: The promise walks into the temple.
note_body: Isaiah said that when God comes to save, blind eyes will open and lame feet will leap. In the cleansed temple courts that day quietly arrives — the blind and the lame come to Jesus, and He heals them.
lens_gloss: to tend, care for, heal — the cleansed court becomes a clinic where mercy does its quiet work.

note_title: Ask what I shall give thee.
note_body: At Gibeon God invited Solomon to name his desire out loud, and on the Jerusalem road Jesus makes the same offer to two ambitious fishermen. God has never been afraid of our wanting — He asks for it plainly, because honest desire is where His deeper work begins.
lens_gloss: to will, to want; Jesus dignifies desire by asking it to stand up and speak plainly.

note_title: Back to the beginning on purpose.
note_body: When hearts had hardened, Jesus did not lower the standard — He reached past Moses' concession all the way back to Eden's one-flesh design. Grace does not settle for what brokenness normalized; it remembers what God originally desired.
lens_gloss: hardness of heart — a heart dried stiff; what Moses accommodated, Jesus came to soften.

note_title: Peter sums up the whole story.
note_body: What happens to one tormented boy in Luke, Peter later preaches as the pattern of everything: Jesus "went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil." His authority is not an occasional miracle — it is who He is, everywhere He goes.
lens_gloss: to rebuke with authority, to command silence — one word from Jesus ends what tormented the child.

note_body: They asked whether healing was lawful so they could accuse; Jesus asked whether the sabbath was for saving life or destroying it — and then healed the man in front of them all. Mercy under criticism does not go silent; it asks the truer question and acts.
lens_gloss: to accuse, to prosecute; mercy does its work under courtroom eyes and does not flinch.

note_body: The mountain-moving faith of Mark grows in the soil of John's upper room — abide in me, let my words abide in you, then ask. Prayer stops wavering when the one praying has stopped living divided from the Vine.
lens_gloss: to be divided in judgment, to waver — doubt as a heart split against its own prayer.

note_body: Moses told Israel to keep their souls diligently, lest what their eyes had seen slip from their hearts — and the risen Jesus tells Sardis the same: remember what you received, hold fast. Forgetting has always been the quiet door that loss walks through.
lens_gloss: to keep on remembering — memory practiced as a discipline that keeps the lamp of watchfulness lit.

note_title: The weeping prophet, the weeping Christ.
note_body: Jeremiah was told to take up lamentation over a generation that refused the LORD, and Jesus' hardest warnings in Matthew 23 dissolve into that same grief. Truth-telling and tears belong together — judgment announced by a voice that is breaking.
lens_gloss: a generation — the living company standing together at a crossroads, warned in love before the reckoning.

note_title: The glory can leave the building.
note_body: Ezekiel watched the glory of God lift up from a temple whose stones still stood, and Mark shows the disciples admiring those stones while the Glory Himself is walking out the gate. Buildings impress; only Presence holds.
lens_gloss: a stone — massive, admired, seemingly permanent, yet unable to hold what only Presence holds.

note_title: Peace to the far and near.
note_body: The LORD says He Himself creates the greeting — "Peace, peace to him that is far off, and to him that is near" — and Jesus puts that very word in His messengers' mouths at the doorstep. We carry the peace; we were never asked to force it.
lens_gloss: worthy, literally "of matching weight" — a house whose welcome balances the gift being offered.

note_body: John's friends bury their teacher and go straight to tell Jesus; Stephen's friends carry him to burial with great lamentation. From the beginning, God's people have been permitted to grieve loudly and bring the whole sorrow to the Lord.
lens_gloss: to report, to carry news — grief's first faithful errand is bringing the whole story to Jesus.

note_title: The lips that should keep knowledge.
note_body: Malachi says a priest's lips should guard knowledge, for people seek truth at his mouth — yet the temple leaders answer the Truth Himself with "we cannot tell." Their evasion is not humility; it is an office abandoned, and Jesus declines to reward it.
lens_gloss: to know — their "we do not know" was not ignorance but refusal dressed as caution.

note_title: A psalm held out like hope.
note_body: Jesus leaves Jerusalem with the festival psalm on His lips — "Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the LORD" — not as a farewell but as the password of His return. The song they sang at the gates is the welcome He is still waiting to hear.
lens_gloss: "the Coming One" — even after rejection, Jesus is still on the way; hope's sentence is unfinished.

note_body: John writes from Patmos as a brother inside the trouble, and Paul preaches the same road — through much tribulation into the kingdom. Endurance is not a lonely assignment; it is company kept in Jesus.
lens_gloss: a sharer together with — John claims no platform above the suffering, only a place beside it in Jesus.

note_title: The prophet saw that sky, too.
note_body: Zechariah promised the LORD would be seen over His people, sudden as lightning with a trumpet sounding; Jesus says His coming will fill the sky the same way. What God makes that visible, His children do not have to chase through rumors.
lens_gloss: lightning — a flash that fills the sky from east to west; when Christ comes, no one will need a rumor.

note_title: Endure the end, receive the crown.
note_body: On the Mount of Olives Jesus says the one who endures to the end shall be saved; from heaven the risen Christ finishes the sentence — be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. The endurance He asks for is endurance He Himself rewards.
lens_gloss: to remain under — endurance that stays put beneath the load without turning bitter, held by the name it suffers for.

note_body: Malachi closes the older covenant promising one who turns the hearts of fathers and children back toward each other; Jesus confirms it — Elias truly comes to restore all things. Restoration is not a new idea God had late; it is the promise He never stopped keeping.
lens_gloss: to set back in place — restoration that returns what was tangled to the order God first intended.

note_title: The fig tree and ten cities.
note_body: Proverbs says the one who tends the fig tree eats its fruit, and the servant who waits on his master shall be honored; Jesus says the same in a king's voice — faithful in a very little, given ten cities. Heaven has always honored quiet tending.
lens_gloss: faithful, trustworthy — proven reliable enough to lean on; the quality Jesus praises before He ever measures size.

note_title: A prophet's room, a prophet's reward.
note_body: The Shunammite woman made room for Elisha simply because he was a man of God, and the reward that came back was a son in her arms. Jesus says that arithmetic still stands: receive one who carries His work, and heaven counts you into the blessing.
lens_gloss: to receive, welcome — opening the door as an act of faith; heaven counts hospitality to His servants as service to Him.

note_title: Set not your heart upon them.
note_body: David warns that when riches increase, the heart must not settle on them; Jesus watches a rich man walk away sorrowful and names how hard that settling is to undo. Both verses aim at the grip, not the gold.
lens_gloss: riches — literally 'things one uses'; the danger Jesus names is when the things we use quietly begin to use us.

note_title: God had already commanded a widow.
note_body: Before Elijah ever reached Zarephath, God had appointed a household to sustain him; Jesus sends His disciples the same way — seek out the worthy home and abide there. Discernment is not suspicion; it is trusting that God has gone ahead and prepared the welcome.
lens_gloss: worthy — what weighs enough on the scale; discernment weighs where welcome is genuine before the servant settles in.

note_title: Not good — heaven said it first.
note_body: The disciples grumble that it is not good to marry; Eden remembers God saying it is not good for man to be alone. Jesus is not making covenant harder than grace can carry — He is calling it back to the goodness God built into it.
lens_gloss: it is advantageous, profitable — the disciples calculate marriage like profit and loss; Jesus answers calculation with covenant.

note_title: The cup taken from our hand.
note_body: Isaiah promises God will take the cup of trembling out of His people's hand; in Mark, Jesus asks two ambitious brothers whether they can drink the cup in His. He drinks what we could not, so every request for a throne must first pass through His cup.
lens_gloss: cup — the appointed portion one must drink; Jesus asks whether they know what fills His before they ask for thrones.

note_title: Accepted according to what you have.
note_body: Paul says a willing heart is accepted according to what a person has, not what they have not; the two-talent servant proves it, welcomed with the very same joy as the five. God measures faithfulness against capacity, never against somebody else's story.
lens_gloss: talent — a weight of treasure worth years of wages; the amounts differ, but the Master's 'well done' does not.

note_title: The Shepherd who carries the carriers.
note_body: Isaiah shows the Shepherd gathering lambs in His arms and gently leading those that are with young; Peter names Him the Chief Shepherd who appears with an unfading crown. The One over the flock tends the ones doing the tending — no hidden labor escapes His bosom.
lens_gloss: Chief Shepherd — the ranking Shepherd over every under-shepherd; no hidden hour of flock work escapes His eye.

note_body: Isaiah told Zion to look up — salvation comes, and his reward is with him; the risen Jesus takes those very words on His own lips at the Bible's closing page. The hope is not vague: the Rewarder Himself is what arrives.
lens_gloss: reward, wages — recompense carried in the Rewarder's own hand; what He brings at His coming is Himself.

note_body: Jesus warns of a master arriving in an hour the servant does not expect, and He says it again to sleepy Sardis — if thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief. The unexpected hour is not a trap; it is a mirror for what the heart does in the dark.
lens_gloss: to watch toward, expect — the leaning-forward posture the servant abandoned; hearts show themselves when they stop expecting the master's return.

note_body: The Sadducees walk in already certain there is no resurrection; Paul follows that assumption to its end — if the dead do not rise, then Christ is not risen. Some questions are not seeking an answer, and Jesus meets them with the truth anyway.
lens_gloss: a standing up again — resurrection; the rising the Sadducees ruled out before they ever finished their question.

note_body: The five-talent servant lays his gain at the master's feet, naming first what he was given; Paul does the same math — I laboured more abundantly, yet not I, but the grace of God. Fruit held up in thanksgiving never curdles into pride.
lens_gloss: to gain as profit — increase that flows from the Master's trust, so the gain comes home as gratitude.

note_title: The quiet Servant, foretold and walking.
note_body: Isaiah promised a Servant who would not cry out or lift His voice in the street, and Matthew quotes that very prophecy right after Jesus charges the crowds to keep silent. The Son's quietness was not weakness — it was fulfillment.
lens_gloss: visible, out in the open — Jesus declines display until the Father's hour, walking straight down Isaiah's quiet prophecy.

note_body: Mark tells how John was bound for telling a king the truth; Matthew shows what the prisoner did with his chains — he heard of the works of Christ and sent his hard questions straight to Jesus. Faithful courage is not the absence of a cell; it is where the heart turns inside one.
lens_gloss: prison, a guarded watch-house — John waits under guard, yet no watched cell can stop questions traveling to Jesus.

note_body: Matthew hears Jesus say the Son of man is come to save that which was lost; Luke hears Him say it standing under Zacchaeus' roof — come to seek and to save. The mission is not a slogan; it walks into houses and calls people by name.
lens_gloss: the lost — what has wandered off and is perishing; in Jesus' mouth the word holds both danger and belonging.

note_title: The Song of Moses, still aching.
note_body: Moses sang of a perverse and crooked generation that grieved the God who carried them; Jesus takes up the old ache — O faithless and perverse generation — yet His very next words are, Bring thy son hither. The grief is ancient, and so is the mercy.
lens_gloss: to bear with, hold up under — even His grieved 'how long' keeps carrying them while He calls the child near.

note_body: Jesus told His disciples that fleeing one city means carrying the word to another, and Acts shows the church doing exactly that — scattered abroad, preaching everywhere they went. In His hands, even a retreat becomes a sowing.
lens_gloss: to flee — in Jesus' instruction not cowardice but strategy; a moving servant is still a sent one.

note_title: Sinai's thunder in a Savior's voice.
note_body: The seventh commandment stands in a few stone-cut words; Jesus takes it deeper, naming covenant betrayal as adultery committed against her — the wounded one God sees. Faithfulness is not cold law; it is the Lord defending a heart.
lens_gloss: to commit adultery — covenant betrayal; Jesus adds 'against her,' giving the wound a face God Himself defends.

note_body: The master returns after a long time and takes account with his servants; Paul says plainly that we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ. The Judge is the same Lord who did the entrusting, which makes the review family business, not a cold audit.
lens_gloss: to take up accounts together — a settling done face to face with the Master in the room, not from far away.

note_title: Blot me — I will not blot.
note_body: Moses stood in the breach and offered, blot me out of Thy book for their sake; Jesus, who actually bore the being cut off, promises the overcomer, I will not blot out his name. What the mediator on Sinai could only offer, the Mediator on Calvary secured.
lens_gloss: to wipe away, erase — Jesus' promise doubles the negative: never, no never, will the overcomer's name be wiped.

note_body: Matthew and Mark each record that after the feeding, Jesus sent the crowd away full and stepped into the boat. Being released is not being rejected — the mercy that fed them was already moving toward the next shore.
lens_gloss: to release, send away — a letting go of the fed and blessed, not a rejection of the loved.

note_title: Love that argued with the cross.
note_body: Mark tells us Peter rebuked Jesus; Matthew preserves the very words — Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee. It sounded like protection, but it was fear pleading against the only road that saves.
lens_gloss: open, plain speech — Jesus hid nothing about the cross; it was fear, not the Master, that pulled aside to whisper.

note_body: Jesus names Himself the sower of the good seed; Paul shrinks the workers down to size — who is Paul, who is Apollos, but ministers as the Lord gave. The field never belonged to the field hands, and that is the workers' rest.
lens_gloss: to sow, scatter seed — the Sower owns the harvest; workers scatter what He supplies and can sleep without anxiety.

note_title: Four verbs, from hillside to table.
note_body: On the hillside Jesus took, gave thanks, brake, and gave; in the upper room He does the same four things with the bread that is His body. Every thanksgiving over not-enough was rehearsing the Table where He Himself became enough.
lens_gloss: to give thanks — the word behind 'Eucharist'; Jesus thanks first over scarce bread and sees the multiplying after.

note_title: A gesture that releases, not retaliates.
note_body: What Jesus commanded on the road, Paul lived out in Corinth — he shook his raiment, declared himself clean, and walked on to the next assignment. The dust comes off so the grudge never settles in.
lens_gloss: to shake out, shake off — a decisive letting-go that leaves judgment in God's hands instead of carrying it down the road with you.

note_title: The songbook already knew the ending.
note_body: The rejection the builders were plotting had been written down and answered a thousand years before, in a psalm Israel sang at every feast. Jesus simply opens their own hymnal — God had always planned to crown the stone they refused.
lens_gloss: to reject after inspection — the builders examined Him and voted no, and God overruled their verdict with a cornerstone.

note_title: Two gates, one call to gather.
note_body: Moses stood in the gate of the camp crying, "Who is on the LORD's side?" and the sons of Levi gathered themselves to him. Jesus stands in the middle of your scattered life making the same call — gathering to Him is the only alternative to drifting apart.
lens_gloss: to gather together into one — Jesus draws scattered lives into one fold; standing neutral quietly scatters what He came to gather.

note_body: Jesus says "I come quickly," and Paul shows what that does to a heart that believes it: "Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand." His nearness makes readiness look like gentleness, not panic.
lens_gloss: quickly, soon, without delay — a nearness meant to keep the heart awake and tender, never clenched in fear.

note_title: Guilt writes its own ghost story.
note_body: Joseph's brothers walked into a house of kindness and read it as a trap, because a guilty conscience mis-tells every mercy. Herod does the same — he hears of Jesus and can only imagine his sin come back to haunt him.
lens_gloss: to raise, to waken — Herod borrows resurrection language from his guilt; only Jesus fills that word with hope instead of dread.

note_title: Measured by the same giving hand.
note_body: The master hands out talents to each servant according to ability, and Paul says grace is given to every one of us according to the measure of Christ's gift. Nothing entrusted to you is random, and nothing entrusted to you is small.
lens_gloss: a talent — a whole weight of silver, years of wages; even the servant given "one" was holding a fortune from the Master's hand.

note_body: Jesus asks His slow disciples if they are still without understanding, and Hebrews meets believers who "have need that one teach you again" the first principles. In Christ's school, repeating a lesson is mercy, not expulsion.
lens_gloss: not yet put together — not stupidity but pieces still unjoined; Jesus keeps teaching until the truth connects.

note_title: Trust is tested before it is given.
note_body: Jesus says of the confident claimants, "believe him not," and John turns the command into a practice: believe not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they are of God. Discernment is how love guards its trust for Christ alone.
lens_gloss: to trust, to lean your weight on — trust is too precious to hand to every urgent voice; Jesus commands it kept for Him.

note_body: Jesus asks whose son the Christ is, then opens the psalm where David calls his own descendant "my Lord," seated at God's right hand. The answer was waiting in the songbook all along — greater than lineage, enthroned by the Father.
lens_gloss: the Anointed One, Messiah — not a topic for opinion polls but God's appointed King, asking your life to agree with His title.

note_title: The fish's belly preaches the tomb.
note_body: The LORD prepared the fish, and Jonah's three days in its belly became the very sign Jesus claims for Himself. What looks like burial is sometimes God preparing a resurrection.
lens_gloss: a sign — a God-given marker pointing beyond itself; Jonah's three dark days point straight to an empty tomb.

note_title: Wisdom that will not be cornered.
note_body: Isaiah promised a Servant who would deal prudently and be exalted. In the temple that prudence answers a trap with a question, turning the light on every heart standing around Him.
lens_gloss: authority — the rightful power to act; Jesus' authority is not granted by committees, it flows from who He is.

note_title: The Healer of the psalm has feet.
note_body: David blessed the LORD "who healeth all thy diseases," and in Galilee the crowds lay every kind of brokenness at Jesus' feet and find that same LORD tending them in person. The covenant Healer now has a lap to be laid before.
lens_gloss: to tend, care for, heal — hands-on restoring care; Jesus does not process crowds, He tends the wounds set before Him.

note_title: Two apostles weigh the same scale.
note_body: Peter stands as witness of Christ's sufferings and partaker of the glory that shall be revealed; Paul does the arithmetic out loud — present sufferings are not worthy to be compared with that glory. Same scale, same verdict, from two men who bled for it.
lens_gloss: witness — one who saw and can testify; Peter's authority rests not on rank but on what he beheld of Christ's sufferings.

note_title: The demand comes with a supply.
note_body: The lawyer asks which commandment is great, and Jesus answers with total love for God and neighbor. Romans tells how such love becomes possible — God sheds His own love abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost, supplying what He commands.
lens_gloss: commandment — a charge entrusted to you; the great charge is not a rule to check off but a love to live inside.

note_title: A pinch is never just a pinch.
note_body: Jesus warns of the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod, and Paul states the kitchen fact plainly: a little leaven leavens the whole lump. Hidden influence never stays small — it spreads until the whole loaf tastes of it.
lens_gloss: leaven — a hidden ferment working silently through the whole batch; influence spreads whether or not it is ever named.

note_body: When the leaders demand Jesus hush the little ones, He opens Psalm 8 — God ordained praise from the mouths of babes to still the enemy. The children's temple song was prophecy coming true out loud.
lens_gloss: to fit together, bring to completion — God builds finished, perfected praise out of the smallest voices in the room.

note_title: A coronation psalm finds its King.
note_body: God promised in Psalm 89 to make David's heir His firstborn, higher than the kings of the earth. Revelation greets the risen Jesus as exactly that — firstborn from the dead, prince of earth's kings, wearing the old promise with scars of love.
lens_gloss: firstborn — first out of the grave and heir over every throne; His resurrection is a birthright He shares with His family.

note_title: Her cry landed on an old promise.
note_body: The psalm says the LORD will fulfil the desire of them that fear Him and will hear their cry; Jesus says, "be it unto thee even as thou wilt." Her persistent cry found the God who had already promised to hear it.
lens_gloss: faith — trust that keeps holding on through silence and delay; hers was called great by the only Judge whose verdict matters.

note_title: Behind the trap, a wounded covenant.
note_body: The Pharisees frame divorce as a debate point to catch Jesus, but Malachi had already shown God's heart — He hates treacherous putting away because it covers violence with a garment. Jesus answers the trap by defending covenant love.
lens_gloss: to test with intent to trap — their question wore a robe of theology over a snare, and Jesus answered the heart anyway.

note_body: The ruler asks what he must do to inherit eternal life and walks away heavy; the Philippian jailer asks nearly the same question and hears, "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ." Eternal life is received, not achieved.
lens_gloss: to inherit — to receive as an heir; an inheritance comes by relationship and grace, never as wages for work performed.

note_body: Isaiah saw a root of Jesse raised as a banner the Gentiles would seek, and Matthew declares it happening — in Jesus' name the nations set their hope. Nobody you have quietly written off stands outside that reach.
lens_gloss: to hope, to set confident expectation — the whole expectation of the nations hangs on one trustworthy Name.

note_title: Exiles and disciples, same first warning.
note_body: Jeremiah told the exiles not to let the prophets and dreamers among them deceive while they waited on God's promise. Jesus gives His waiting church the same opening word — take heed, stay on the road, let no one lead you off.
lens_gloss: to lead astray, cause to wander — deception is less a lie believed than a road quietly left; Jesus guards the road.

note_body: In both scenes the examiners arrive from Jerusalem, and Luke adds the wonder: while the critics sat watching, the power of the Lord was present to heal. Scrutiny never made Jesus small, frantic, or unkind.
lens_gloss: scribe — a professional keeper of the letter; expertise can inspect the Word made flesh up close and still miss Him.

note_body: The angel declares these sayings faithful and true, and Peter explains why — prophecy never came by the will of man, but holy men spake as they were moved by the Holy Ghost. God's promises bear weight because God authored them.
lens_gloss: faithful, trustworthy — words that hold firm when you put the full weight of a fear or a decision on them.

note_body: Isaiah promised a day when blind eyes open and stopped ears unstop, and Matthew shows the man both seeing and speaking the moment Jesus heals him. The promised age is not a date on a calendar — it is a Person in the room.
lens_gloss: mute, dulled, blunted — a life gone silent; when Jesus heals, shut mouths and closed eyes open together.

note_body: Jesus says it is better to enter the kingdom with one eye than to keep what destroys you; Paul shows the same math from the inside — what things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ. What Jesus removes always costs less than what He gives.
lens_gloss: to trip, to ensnare — the word behind "offend" is a baited trap-stick; Jesus says no trap is worth carrying into eternity.

note_title: The staff fails; the Master comes.
note_body: Gehazi laid the prophet's staff on the child, and there was neither voice nor hearing; the disciples tried and could not cure the boy. Borrowed power runs out — the need must be carried to Jesus Himself, and He does not fail it.
lens_gloss: to be able, to have power — Scripture honestly records the "could not" so we bring our lack back to the One who can.

note_title: A steward's clock, a mother's lamp.
note_body: Jesus honors the steward who gives the household their portion of meat in due season, and Proverbs had already painted her — rising while it is yet night to give meat to her household. Faithfulness looks like ordinary provision, on time, with love.
lens_gloss: household manager, steward — trusted with someone else's house; faithfulness is measured in ordinary portions served on time.

note_body: In the temple court the leaders calculate their answer to dodge it, and in John's Gospel Jesus asks it straight out: if the truth is standing in front of you, why don't you believe? Both scenes show that the real obstacle to obedience is rarely evidence — it is what believing would cost us.
lens_gloss: to reason back and forth within oneself — the self-protective calculating that weighs consequences instead of answering truth plainly.

note_title: An old psalm on the Jericho road.
note_body: Centuries before, the psalmist prayed the same plain sentence — open my eyes — asking to see wonders in God's Word. On the Jericho road two blind men pray it to the Word made flesh, and He stops, touches, and answers in person.
lens_gloss: to open what was shut — Scripture's word for opened eyes, opened doors, opened heavens; true sight always begins as God's act.
